articleTitle: Superconducting transmission lines of controllable properties
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Microwave Applications of High-Temperature Superconductors
abstract: It is well known that the measured properties of superconductors are sensitive to magnetic field, whether generated by self-currents or externally applied. The authors suggest that it may be possible to take advantage of this sensitivity, by applying it to develop microwave components whose characteristics can be varied by an externally applied control field. This field could be produced by a current-carrying conductor lying near the component whose properties are to be controlled. They envisage this technique as being applicable to structures containing superconductors in bulk or thick-film form, as well as to thin-film systems. It appears straightforward to switch high-T/sub c/ material between superconducting and normal states by applying a magnetic field from a coil or other conductor. Digital control of this form might be used for phase shifting, for switching delay elements or for signal routing, preferably with balanced circuitry to maintain impedance values. The development of continuously variable (analogue) control will make it possible to control the electrical length of delay lines and sections of transmission line, and the properties of other passive devices including filters and resonators.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Supercooled and superconducting small loop antenna
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Microwave Applications of High-Temperature Superconductors
abstract: A small loop antenna constructed with YBCO superconducting wire is demonstrated. The radiation efficiency shows a 5db improvement over an equivalent supercooled copper antenna. In addition, as the power input to the antenna is increased an increase in the antenna conduction losses is observed as the superconductor critical current is reached.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: High temperature superconductors at high frequencies
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Microwave Applications of High-Temperature Superconductors
abstract: Many of the high frequency applications of superconductors depend on their low high frequency losses. However, the much weaker frequency dependence for normal metals means that at high enough frequencies the surface impedance of say cold copper is comparable to that of the superconductor. This crossover frequency is a simple measure of material performance. It should rise as the sample is cooled further. At present the best in-situ films can have crossover frequencies well over 300 GHz when measured at 77 K. Even post-annealed films can get above 50 GHz, depending on the superconductor orientation and the presence of second phases. At lower frequencies the margin of advantage over normal metals increases. There is every reason to believe that the present day performance is not fundamental, and that further improvements in the crystallinity and purity of the films will be reflected in their high frequency performance.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An overview of superconducting nonlinear-circuit simulation
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Microwave Applications of High-Temperature Superconductors
abstract: To assist the development of superconducting millimetre and submillimetre-wave receivers, the authors have devised algorithms and written in the C programming language modular software for analysing the small-signal, large-signal and noise behaviour of SIS tunnel-junction circuits. Typical applications include the modelling of mixers, subharmonic mixers and direct detectors. To analyse the complex behaviour of a nonlinear SIS tunnel-junction circuit, it is first necessary to model the large-signal steady-state dynamics of the circuit; the underlying system of equations can then be perturbed, either numerically or analytically, to gain information about the linear relationships between signal and noise variables. A general-purpose simulator must therefore be capable of solving large systems of coupled nonlinear equations.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Microwave applications of high temperature superconductors based on the Josephson effect and tunnelling
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Microwave Applications of High-Temperature Superconductors
abstract: Superconductors have proven potential for microwave applications, both for passive structures like cavities, filters and transmission lines, and for active devices, such as mixers, detectors, amplifiers and signal sources. The author examines the present status and prospects of such active devices based on high transition temperature (high-T/sub c/) superconducting tunnel junctions.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Microwave potentialities of high temperature superconductors
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Microwave Applications of High-Temperature Superconductors
abstract: The advent of materials which superconduct above liquid nitrogen temperatures has, therefore, been accompanied by a revival of interest in potential superconducting device applications at microwave frequencies. These applications fall into three categories: (1) zero resistance devices (i) microwave resonators (ii) transmission lines (iii) antennae (2) Josephson devices (i) A to D converters (ii) frequency mixers (3) EM devices (i) microwave sensors (ii) photon detectors.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Microwave properties of Hi-Tc thick film superconductors
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Microwave Applications of High-Temperature Superconductors
abstract: Work at STL is focussed on developing an understanding of high frequency properties of thick film high T/sub c/ superconductors and providing design rules for the fabrication of superconducting RF and microwave components and systems. Current work is directed towards the fabrication of components for which present performance is conductor loss limited and the testing of these at frequencies around 1 GHz. In particular the aim is to assess the performance of superconducting transmission lines and resonators formed from transmission lines.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Modelling and applications of superconductive transmission lines at micro and millimetric wave frequencies
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Microwave Applications of High-Temperature Superconductors
abstract: The first objective of this paper is to present a new transmission line model which, not only realistically describes the interconnect transmission lines in monolithic integrated circuits but can also be used to study limitations associated with losses, reflections and discontinuities. The second objective of the paper is to assess the use of superconductors as interconnect material in future IC technology by studying ultrafast propagation in a realistic interconnect example selected from the practical prototype shown. The results identify the features of present VlSI IC technology which may be the problem in the picosecond regime.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
